approval_required_for: Any change to the approved decoder-block architecture or operator order.
Any change to residual buffering policy, pipeline structure, stream ordering, transfer layout, or memory layout rather than a bounded implementation correction that restores the existing contract.
Any change to numeric policy, cast points, rounding, saturation, resolved atol, rtol, or max_mismatch_fraction during the repair loop.
Any major template change or expansion of accelerator scope to embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, or other model-tail work.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify missing target-model execution, unresolved initial tolerance, incomplete block tensor scope, or semantic-harness generation as a checker/golden-reference capability blocker, not as hardware failure. Do not substitute random, identity/default, sampled-weight, or RTL-derived expected outputs, and do not begin the connected-layer run.
executable_actions.rationale: Functional acceptance needs one immutable identity spanning the complete target decoder-block tensor scope, deterministic input, real target-model execution, numeric comparison policy, resolved tolerance, and generated semantic harness. Expected outputs must never come from random data or the DUT.

consumes: operator-leaf simulator logs and golden reports
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep layer 2 blocked and hand the failing leaf checker evidence to the operator-leaf verification owner. Do not perform independent leaf repair in this role and do not create a reusable leaf certificate without current-contract validation.
executable_actions.rationale: The connected kernel may consume reusable leaf evidence only after all nine leaf stages are aggregated under the current real-weight semantic-evidence contract.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block simulation and localize the contract discrepancy against the approved Stage 3 and Stage 4 artifacts. Do not change model order, residual source, activation semantics, stream order, cast policy, or tolerance to accommodate the generated DUT.
executable_actions.rationale: The connected testbench and kernel contract must bind model ordering, residual identities, branch joins, cast points, stream ordering, and checker aliases to one generated implementation before simulation.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not promote and do not proceed to board integration. Send the real simulator log, first failing transaction, boundary trace, and immutable run identity to the contract-guided localization action; do not patch a downstream symptom before finding the earliest causal boundary.
executable_actions.rationale: Dynamic evidence is required to prove connected attention/MLP ordering, residual alignment, stream identity, liveness, transfer completeness, and actual use of every required decoder-block weight.

executable_actions.on_failure: Preserve checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, policy, atol, rtol, max_mismatch_fraction, testbench hashes, and boundary contract. Route the first ordered mismatch to causal localization; never derive or loosen tolerance from DUT output.
executable_actions.rationale: The connected DUT output must be compared with independently executed target-model boundary data under the pre-resolved numeric policy, tolerance, and logical stream order.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep both promotion and higher-layer execution blocked. Do not guess a module or reopen all leaves; request additional bounded boundary instrumentation if the earliest causal violation cannot be established.
executable_actions.rationale: A failed value, order, liveness, transfer, or weight-consumption checker must identify the earliest causal connected boundary before deciding whether the fault belongs to layer-2 integration or contradicts a reusable leaf certificate.

executable_actions.on_failure: Return to localization with the new real-tool evidence. If the proposed fix would change architecture, approved pipeline order, residual buffering policy, stream order, memory layout, numeric policy, tolerance, or a major template, stop and request approval rather than applying the change. A leaf-assigned contradiction must instead follow the explicit operator-leaf backtrack request.
executable_actions.rationale: When localization assigns the earliest violation to connected-layer wiring, buffering, loader binding, or instrumentation, repair only the bounded implementation that violates the already approved contract and rerun the failed real-tool path.

executable_actions.on_failure: Set current_contract_valid=false, keep reuse_allowed=false, and block case_board_interface_discovery and case_multilayer_pipeline. Do not issue a partial certificate or treat artifact presence as validity.
executable_actions.rationale: Promotion requires one checker-bound aggregate proving current lower-layer lineage, connected semantics, immutable identity, independent golden data, resolved numeric comparison, real simulation, complete block-weight consumption, and all required checker passes under evidence contract v2.

observations: The populated sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Historical records therefore create no current SACG-memory blocker.

Stage 3 pipeline checks, Stage 4 parameter checks, and Stage 5 compile, elaboration, contract, and package-static checks passed. These are valid prerequisites but are not functional hardware evidence.

The visible attention dimensions are internally consistent: 14 query heads times head_dim 64 equals hidden_size 896, two KV heads imply a GQA group size of seven, causal attention and RoPE theta 1000000.0 are declared, and the sequence bound is 16.

The declared cast and residual precisions are consistent at the principal joins: the first attention result and original block input are both presented to residual_add_1 at 32-bit precision, while the MLP down projection and first residual result are both presented to residual_add_2 at 32-bit precision.

The required connected semantics are pre-normalized attention followed by the first residual, then pre-normalized gated MLP followed by the second residual: n1=norm1(x), r1=x+attention(n1), n2=norm2(r1), m=down(target_activation(gate(n2))*up(n2)), and y=r1+m. The execution contract must preserve the two residual identities and the common n2 identity across both MLP projection branches.

The candidate has a static data_order_trace_check pass only. Its execution status explicitly requires downstream simulation, so it does not prove dynamic stream identity, branch alignment, transfer count, liveness, or value correctness.
The presence summary confirms nine parameter bindings and nine stage agents, including stage_08_residual_add_2. Details omitted by the role-specific slice are not treated as missing artifacts.

The single-layer DAG has the correct broad order: current operator-leaf evidence, scaffold, connected kernel, functional run, golden comparison, then semantic aggregation. The current operator-leaf certificate and single-layer certificate are both marked missing or stale for the current evidence contract.

The visible DAG names the connected node single_transformer_layer, while this role's acceptance interface also names case_single_transformer_layer. Both identifiers must be bound to the same kernel source hash and run identity rather than being allowed to certify different implementations.

Complete real-weight evidence must cover every tensor required by exactly one target decoder block according to the complete target-checkpoint catalog and bound loader. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail tensors are outside accelerator scope and must remain outside layer acceptance requirements.

The target-model golden must be generated by executing the real target decoder block on the same immutable checkpoint, block index, input stimulus, position/cache state, and sequence configuration used by the DUT. Random generation is permitted only for the input stimulus.

No numeric-comparison result is present. Before simulation acceptance, the current-run tolerance values, or authorized frozen framework loose defaults when current values were initially absent, must be resolved and hashed without reference to DUT output. Those values must then remain immutable throughout repair.

The Stage 5 compile and elaboration success does not demonstrate that the generated DUT consumed checkpoint weights. Acceptance requires executed loader/harness evidence with complete-scope tensor hashes and per-binding consumption proof.

Vivado, exact sample-project wrapper, AXI/DDR, bitstream, and board-runtime execution are later-stage obligations rather than current Stage 6 static risks. They remain blocked by the absent single-layer promotion certificate.
proposed_actions: Freeze the decoder-block semantic identity: checkpoint and complete block tensor catalog, layer index, deterministic input provenance, position/cache state, target-model boundary outputs, numeric policy and resolved tolerance, and semantic-testbench hashes.
Execute and validate the current-contract operator-leaf prerequisite; route any leaf failure to its owner rather than repairing it within the connected-layer role.

Materialize the connected merge-boundary contract with residual fork/join identities, GQA and RoPE metadata, target activation ordering, cast points, stream identities, and an explicit alias between case_single_transformer_layer and single_transformer_layer.
Run a real connected-layer simulator with deadlock, transfer-count, data-order, and complete weight-consumption instrumentation.
Compare the DUT boundary output against the independent target-model boundary output using the frozen numeric policy and tolerance.

On failure, localize the earliest causal boundary, issue either a current-layer retry or a trace-bound leaf backtrack, perform only contract-restoring bounded repair, and rerun the failed checker set.
Aggregate immutable identities and executed evidence into a current-contract-valid single-layer promotion certificate before releasing board-interface discovery or multi-layer generation.
risks: Current layer-2 blocker: artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate is absent or stale for the current contract, so the connected-layer run cannot rely on reusable lower-layer closure yet.
Current layer-2 blocker: artifact.stage7.single_layer_promotion_certificate is absent, and every required single-layer execution node is still marked required_pending_execution.

A branch-identity error could feed norm1 output or a reordered stream into residual_add_1 instead of the original x stream, or feed different n2 transactions into gate and up projections. Static module presence would not detect these failures.
A residual latency or FIFO mismatch could pair attention or MLP output with the wrong tx_id, tile_id, logical index, token, or lane while preserving apparently legal valid/ready behavior.

A GQA mapping, RoPE position, causal-mask, bounded-cache-state, or sequence-length mismatch could produce numerically plausible but model-inconsistent outputs unless the target-model reference and DUT share immutable boundary metadata.
A target-activation or gate/up multiplication-order mismatch at stage_06_activation_mul could survive independent projection checks and first appear only at the connected MLP merge.
A manifest-only weight claim could conceal omitted, defaulted, sampled, misaddressed, or unread tensors. Promotion requires complete catalog coverage plus executed DUT consumption evidence.
The single_transformer_layer versus case_single_transformer_layer naming distinction could create split evidence unless an explicit alias and common source/run hash are certified.

Changing checkpoint, stimulus, reference output, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench, or boundary contract after a failure would contaminate the repair loop and invalidate comparison evidence.
Reopening an independently passed leaf without a connected-layer trace identifying the earliest contradictory leaf boundary would violate the three-layer repair policy and this role's authority.
